prompt.context_jp: ナギサが姿を消してから、もう三日___経っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサが姿を消してから、もう三日___経っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the opening narration about three days having passed.

feedback.correct_en: The chapter opens by introducing a new fact to the reader — that three days have passed. New information presented for the first time takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat '三日' as an already-established topic, which doesn't fit this scene-setting opener. を doesn't work with the intransitive 経つ.

contrast_examples.en: As for three days — they've already passed. (contrastive/known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 連絡___一切なく、メイは薫の店の隅の席で、料理に箸をつけることもできずに座っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 連絡___一切なく
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits: '[contact] was entirely absent'?

feedback.correct_en: は marks 連絡 as the topic under negation — 'as for contact, there was none at all.' Japanese strongly prefers は when stating the absence of something expected.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like it's newly introducing 連絡 as subject, but here the narrator is commenting on its absence in a known situation.

contrast_examples.en: There's no contact at all. (expected thing absent)

prompt.context_jp: 付き合いの長い友の目には、その沈黙___いちばん見ていられないものだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: その沈黙___いちばん見ていられないものだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the こそ+ga pattern isolating 'that silence' as the single most unbearable thing?

feedback.correct_en: こそが singles out 'that silence' exhaustively — of all things, THIS is the one he couldn't bear to see. Exhaustive-listing が pairs naturally with こそ.
feedback.incorrect_en: こそは is possible in some contrastive patterns but doesn't deliver the 'it is precisely X' identification that this sentence builds toward.

contrast_examples.en: This time for sure I'll succeed. (contrastive emphasis)

prompt.context_jp: 「ナギサさんのほうに 問題___あったんじゃない？」
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサさんのほうに 問題___あったんじゃない？
prompt.prompt_en: Kaoru is floating a new hypothesis. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Kaoru is introducing a brand-new idea — that a problem might exist on Nagisa's side. 問題がある/あった with existential ある takes が when the issue is newly proposed.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose 問題 as a known topic already under discussion, but Kaoru is raising it for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: As for the problem, it's already solved. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「なるよ マリッジブルー___ 性別は関係ないから」
prompt.prompt_jp: マリッジブルー___ 性別は関係ないから
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle links 'cold feet' with 'gender is unrelated'?

feedback.correct_en: 関係ない takes に to mark the thing something is unrelated TO. 'As for gender, it's unrelated to marriage blues.'
feedback.incorrect_en: で would read as location/means, and を doesn't pair with the intransitive 関係ない.

prompt.context_jp: 瀬川が一日五通のメールを送り続けていたと聞かされた瞬間、メイの胸の奥で何か___弾んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: メイの胸の奥で何か___弾んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Something stirred in Mei's chest. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: 何か (something indefinite) nearly always takes が — it's unidentified new information appearing on the scene. The narrator is reporting a fresh, unnamed feeling.
feedback.incorrect_en: 何か+は is ungrammatical here; indefinite 'something' can't be a known topic. を doesn't fit the intransitive 弾む.

prompt.context_jp: どんな相手であれ、最初の五分___制すれば、次の五分にはつながる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 最初の五分___制すれば
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits with 制する (to dominate/control)?

feedback.correct_en: 制する is a transitive verb meaning 'to control/dominate.' Its direct object — here 'the first five minutes' — takes を.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make '五分' the subject that controls something, flipping the meaning. に doesn't fit this verb at all.

prompt.context_jp: 「患者さんのこと___一番に考えてる 気持ちは 同じだと思うんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 患者さんのこと___一番に考えてる
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks what everyone is thinking about first?

feedback.correct_en: 考える takes を for its object. Segawa is saying everyone is thinking ABOUT the patient first — the patient is the thing being considered.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'the patient' the one doing the thinking. に is not used with 考える in this meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 君のことを考えている。

prompt.context_jp: 「相原さん___ 自分のせいで あなたが出てったんだと とても落ち込んでいました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 相原さん___ 自分のせいで あなたが出てったんだと とても落ち込んでいました
prompt.prompt_en: Tadokoro is telling Nagisa about Aihara. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Aihara is the topic Tadokoro is reporting on. Note the embedded clause already uses あなたが出てった — the internal subject is marked with が, while the outer topic 相原さん takes は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would compete with the inner あなたが and lose the topic-comment structure Tadokoro needs to deliver the news clearly.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は、妹が来たと言った。
contrast_examples.en: He said his sister came. (outer topic は, inner subject が)
He said it was his sister. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 「俺じゃないんですよ 相原さんには あなた___必要なんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 相原さんには あなた___必要なんです
prompt.prompt_en: Tadokoro insists it's YOU (not me) that Aihara needs. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: This is exhaustive-listing が: 'it is YOU — and no one else — that she needs.' Tadokoro has just denied himself as the answer, so が identifies the one true answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would merely topicalize 'you,' losing the exclusive 'it is precisely you' punch Tadokoro's confrontation needs.

contrast_examples.jp: あなたが必要なんです。

prompt.context_jp: 「たった3日___ 出ていかれちゃったんだって？」
prompt.prompt_jp: たった3日___ 出ていかれちゃったんだって？
prompt.prompt_en: Yui teases: 'he walked out after just three days?' Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: で marks the time span within which the event completed — 'within just 3 days.' It emphasizes how quickly the whole thing wrapped up.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a point in time ('on day 3'), not a duration. を doesn't fit this intransitive event.

contrast_examples.en: I met (him) on the 3rd. (point in time)

prompt.context_jp: 「もともとさ 決まった形なんて___ないんだから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 決まった形なんて___ないんだから
prompt.prompt_en: Mother says there's no set form for marriage. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: With なんて and negation, は is natural — it topicalizes 'a set form' and denies its existence in a generalizing, contrastive way: 'as for a fixed form, there's no such thing.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が+ない exists but doesn't mesh with なんて's dismissive flavor; the mother is making a broad philosophical statement, not newly introducing an absence.

contrast_examples.en: There's no such thing as a right answer. (dismissive topic)
There IS a right answer. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 「家___も帰らず どこにいるんですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 家___も帰らず どこにいるんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle combines with も to mean 'not even going home'?

feedback.correct_en: 帰る takes に to mark the destination. 家にも帰らず = 'without even returning home,' where にも adds 'not even to this place.'
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks a location of action, not a destination of motion. を with 帰る would mean 'leave from' — the wrong direction.

prompt.context_jp: 「恐らく私___メイさんより 先に死にます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 恐らく私___メイさんより 先に死にます
prompt.prompt_en: Nagisa makes a quiet statement about himself. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Nagisa is introducing himself as topic and giving a comment about his own future — a classic は use for self-reflective declarations.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like exhaustive listing ('I am the one who will die first'), which turns a vulnerable confession into an odd identification claim.

contrast_examples.en: I'll go on ahead. (topic + comment about self)
I'll be the one to go. (I, exclusively)

prompt.context_jp: 「メイさんは 優しくて 負けん気___強いので」
prompt.prompt_jp: 優しくて 負けん気___強いので
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in the 'X is strong' body-part/trait pattern?

feedback.correct_en: In the 'X は Y が + adjective' pattern describing someone's traits, the trait (負けん気) takes が. The larger topic メイさん is already marked with は at the start.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would double-mark topics inside a single clause and break the natural trait-description pattern.

contrast_examples.en: He is tall. (lit. as for him, back is high)
He is expensive/tall. (ambiguous, lacks the trait frame)

prompt.context_jp: 「私にとって一片も悔いのない人生___ これからナギサさんと一緒に 歩いていく人生です」
prompt.prompt_jp: 一片も悔いのない人生___ これからナギサさんと一緒に 歩いていく人生です
prompt.prompt_en: Mei defines what a life without regret means to her. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: This is a defining A は B です sentence: 'A life without regret IS a life walking with you.' は sets up the topic being defined; the predicate completes the definition.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn it into exhaustive listing ('it's the no-regret life that is the one with you'), which is backwards — Mei wants to define, not single out.

contrast_examples.jp: 私の夢は医者になることです。
contrast_examples.en: My dream is to become a doctor. (definition)

prompt.context_jp: 「1日 5通 メール___んです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 1日 5通 メール___んです
prompt.prompt_en: Segawa explains how he got the appointment. Which verb fits with メール?

feedback.correct_en: The source text uses メールしたんです — メールする is the standard denominal verb for 'to email.' It's compact and natural in casual explanation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 送る works grammatically but needs を (メールを送った). やる is too colloquial and awkward here.

contrast_examples.en: I sent emails every day. (needs を)

prompt.context_jp: 「今度から アポのメールは ___にしてください」
prompt.prompt_jp: アポのメールは ___にしてください
prompt.prompt_en: Dr. Sakamoto asks for shorter appointment emails. Which word fits?

feedback.correct_en: 簡潔 (concise/succinct) is the business-register word for well-written brief messages. It's the actual word Dr. Sakamoto uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: 短い just means 'short' in length and lacks the 'well-organized' nuance. 簡単 means 'easy/simple,' which would read as 'make the content simple' — slightly condescending.

prompt.context_jp: Nagisa opens with a formal apology at the door.
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ございません」
prompt.prompt_en: Which fixed phrase does Nagisa use to apologize?

feedback.correct_en: 申し訳ございません is the highest-register fixed apology — the only form that combines with ございません. It fits Nagisa's unfailingly polite speech.
feedback.incorrect_en: ごめんございません and すまないございません are not Japanese — these words don't combine with ございません. Those apologies stay plain-form.

prompt.context_jp: 「結婚って ___の中を 進んでいくようなものよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 結婚って ___の中を 進んでいくようなものよ
prompt.prompt_en: Mother's metaphor for marriage. Which word fits?

feedback.correct_en: 真っ暗闇 (pitch-black darkness) sets up the next line — that partners must light the way for each other. The metaphor only works if the starting point is dark.
feedback.incorrect_en: 真っ白 (pure white) and 明るい道 (bright road) contradict the 'light for each other' moral that follows.

prompt.context_jp: 「お互いに依存するんじゃなくて 足りないところを___いけたら いいと思うんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 足りないところを___いけたら
prompt.prompt_en: Mei describes the kind of partnership she wants. Which verb fits?

feedback.correct_en: 補う (to supplement/make up for) is the idiomatic verb for filling in each other's gaps. It pairs directly with 足りないところ.
feedback.incorrect_en: 隠す ('hide') sounds like concealing flaws from each other. 直す ('fix/correct') implies one partner is faulty and needs repair — the opposite of mutual complementing.

prompt.context_jp: 「あなたは いつも そうやって 私の___を下ろしてしまいますね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私の___を下ろしてしまいますね
prompt.prompt_en: Nagisa's idiomatic thanks: 'you always take X off me.'

feedback.correct_en: 肩の荷を下ろす is a set idiom meaning 'to feel relieved of a burden.' It's exactly what Nagisa feels when Mei refuses to let worries about the future paralyze them.
feedback.incorrect_en: 荷物を下ろす is literal 'put down luggage.' 重さを下ろす isn't idiomatic Japanese.

prompt.context_jp: Dr. Sakamoto softens about his brother, the Pharmacy Director.
prompt.prompt_jp: 「腐っても___」
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the proverb Sakamoto uses about his brother?

feedback.correct_en: 腐っても鯛 ('even rotten, it's still sea bream') is the model. Sakamoto adapts it to 腐っても兄弟 — 'rotten as he may be, he's still my brother' — carrying pride and resignation at once.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other choices don't match what Sakamoto actually says; the story later reveals the Pharmacy Director is literally his brother, which is why this twist on the proverb lands.

contrast_examples.en: Even past its prime, it's still top-grade. (proverb)
Rotten or not, (he's) still my brother. (Sakamoto's twist)

prompt.context_jp: Mei has just told Nagisa over the phone that she's standing in front of his house.
prompt.prompt_en: Which of Mei's responses sounds most natural given her firm-but-gentle stance in this scene?

choices.text: いいです 動かないで
もしよろしければ、そちらで少々お待ちいただけますでしょうか

feedback.correct_en: The source line いいです 動かないで is the natural middle register for this emotional moment — firm enough to stop Nagisa from fleeing again, soft enough to signal she wants to see him.
feedback.incorrect_en: 動くな、待ってろ is barked-command register that doesn't fit Mei's voice. The keigo variant is far too formal for a soon-to-be spouse in an intimate phone call.

prompt.context_jp: Mei's climactic line to Nagisa, echoing Tadokoro's earlier words.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for Mei's confession here?

choices.text: 私も あなたを 手放したくないんです
私も 手放したくないんです あなたを
あなたを 私も 手放したくないんです

feedback.correct_en: The source order — topic/subject (私も) → object (あなたを) → verb — is the neutral, emotionally direct word order. It lets 'you' land right before the verb.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) front-loads the verb and leaves あなたを as an awkward tail, which sounds like a correction. (c) moves the object to front-focus, which would imply contrast ('you specifically, not someone else'), out of place in this gentle climax.

contrast_examples.jp: 私もあなたを愛しています。
あなたを、私も愛しています。

prompt.context_jp: Kaoru teases Mei about Nagisa walking out after 3 days.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best matches the casual, teasing-friend register Kaoru uses?

choices.text: 三日間でクーリング・オフ制度が適用されたのですね
三日のクーリング・オフだな

feedback.correct_en: The source line uses で (duration) + sentence-final か with a trailing pause — the sigh-and-tease register that fits Kaoru's bar banter.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) is full keigo, wrong for a close friend. (c) replaces で with の, which changes it from 'within 3 days' to 'a 3-day cooling-off,' subtly losing the 'wow, that fast' nuance.

prompt.context_jp: Mei comes home and hands Nagisa the eggs she bought.
prompt.prompt_en: Which exchange sounds most natural for this everyday domestic moment?

choices.text: 「おかえりなさい」「はい 卵 買ってきました」
「おかえりなさい」「はい 卵 買っていきました」
「ただいま」「はい 卵 買ってまいりました」

feedback.correct_en: 買ってきました (literally 'bought and came') is the natural way to report bringing something home — the directional てくる points toward the speaker's current location.
feedback.incorrect_en: 買っていきました points away from the current location — wrong when you've just arrived home with the eggs. The third option mismatches the welcome: Nagisa says おかえりなさい, not Mei.

contrast_examples.en: I bought bread (and brought it here).
I bought bread (and took it away).

prompt.context_jp: Mei pressing Nagisa for a proper explanation outside his home.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best matches the quietly firm, polite tone Mei uses?

choices.text: 何も言いたくないなんて 道理が通りません ちゃんと説明してください
黙ってんじゃねえよ、ちゃんと説明しろ
恐れ入りますが、お話を伺えますでしょうか

feedback.correct_en: The source line keeps the です/ます register but pushes with 道理が通りません and the direct 説明してください — firm, not harsh. This is Mei's signature grown-up pressure.
feedback.incorrect_en: (b) switches to rough masculine speech Mei doesn't use. (c) is so softened with keigo that it becomes a polite request, losing the demand for truth.
